info.title: Brand24 API Data
info.description:
Brand24 is a media monitoring and analytics platform that helps organizations understand, measure, and act on online conversations about their brand, products, competitors, and industry.

This API provides access to Brand24's statistics and insights.

## Server-Side Only API

This API must be called from your backend server only. Do not call it from a browser, frontend JavaScript, or mobile app — your API key is a secret and must never be exposed in client-side code.

## Projects Data Structure

Brand24 collects and processes data within projects created in a user's account.

Projects allow you to organize and manage the data about a particular brand, product, competitor, or industry you monitor in Brand24.

Most API endpoints operate within the context of a specific project, so you will typically need to provide a project ID when making requests.

## Base URL

`https://api-data.brand24.com`

## Authentication

All requests must include an `X-Api-Key` HTTP header. Your API key is available at [app.brand24.com/account/integrations-api-data](https://app.brand24.com/account/integrations-api-data).

**Important:** Use the API key only in server-side (backend) code. Never embed it in frontend JavaScript, HTML, or mobile apps. Browser requests will be blocked by CORS.

## Response Format

All endpoints return JSON with a consistent envelope:

- **Success:** `{ "status": "success", "data": { ... } }`
- **Client error (4xx):** `{ "status": "fail", "message": "...", "code": 400 }`
- **Server error (5xx):** `{ "status": "error", "message": "...", "code": 500 }`

## HTTP Status Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Success |
| 400 | Bad request — invalid or missing parameters |
| 401 | Unauthorized — missing or invalid API key |
| 404 | Not found — invalid endpoint URL |
| 500 | Internal server error |

get.description:
Returns project mentions within a selected date range using cursor pagination.

Each result row contains 9 fields:

`date, time, title, content, source, host, category, sentiment, tags`

For ToS-restricted sources (Facebook, Instagram, X/Twitter), text fields are limited:
- Facebook, Instagram: `title`, `content`, `source` are `null`
- X/Twitter: `title` and `content` are `null`, while `source` is `"Tweet-ID: <id>"`

All other sources return full values.

`date_from` and `date_to` are required and inclusive; maximum range depends on the plan.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: ID of your project

parameters.name: date_from
parameters.description: Start of date range. Allowed format: YYYY-MM-DD.

parameters.name: date_to
parameters.description: End of date range. Allowed format: YYYY-MM-DD. Must be equal to or after `date_from`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Default 500, maximum 500.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from the previous response. Treat as a black-box string.

parameters.name: sentiment
parameters.description: Filter by sentiment. Comma-separated values: `positive`, `negative`, `neutral`.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Filter by source category tokens. Comma-separated values.

post.description:
Creates a new monitoring project that collects mentions containing the given keywords.

Use this endpoint to set up a new Brand24 monitoring scope for a brand, product, competitor, or topic.

You can create a project with one or more keywords. For every keyword you can optionally provide `required` words (all must appear alongside the keyword) or `excluded` words (mentions containing these are filtered out).

If you provide a `language` parameter, only mentions in that language are collected. If omitted, mentions in any language are collected.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: Account ID that will own the new project.

parameters.name: project_name
parameters.description: Human-readable name of the project to create.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Language filter for collected mentions. If omitted, mentions in any language are collected. Only one language can be provided.

get.description: Returns anomaly events detected for a given project and date range. Events represent significant spikes or unusual patterns in mention activity, enriched with context such as peak mentions, peak reach, and an AI-generated description. Use this endpoint to explain sudden surges in attention.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: ID of your project

parameters.name: date_from
parameters.description: Start of date range. Allowed format: YYYY-MM-DD. Optional — if omitted, defaults to 31 days before `date_to` (or 31 days ago when both are omitted).

parameters.name: date_to
parameters.description: End of date range. Allowed format: YYYY-MM-DD. Must be equal to or after `date_from` when both are provided. Optional — if omitted, defaults to today.

parameters.name: sort_order
parameters.description: Sort order for returned events by anomaly date.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of events to return.

get.description: Returns AI-detected topics for a given project and date range. Topics represent recurring themes found across mentions, enriched with metrics such as mention count, reach, sentiment breakdown, and share of voice. Use this endpoint to summarize the main themes in the conversation. The `status` field indicates the state of topic analysis: `ok` (data available) or `unavailable` (analysis not ready or not enabled).

get.description: Returns daily project metrics for the selected date range, including mentions count, reach, sentiment ratio and engagement. Both dates are optional — the missing date is inferred from the other (±31 days). When neither date is provided, defaults to the last 31 days. Returns 400 if both dates are provided and the range exceeds 31 days. Optionally, metrics can be filtered by source and include a per-source daily breakdown.

ProjectMentionsListResponse.description:
Each mention contains public fields without the internal mention id. For ToS-restricted sources the `title`, `content` and `source` fields are blanked:

- **Facebook, Instagram** — `title`, `content`, `source` all `null`
- **Twitter / X** — `title` and `content` are `null`; `source` is `"Tweet-ID: <id>"`
- **All other sources** (TikTok, news, blogs, YouTube, Reddit, LinkedIn, …) — full data exposed

items.description: 9-field row for the project mentions response.

date.description: Calendar date the mention was published (Excel column: Date).

time.description: Time of day, HH:MM (Excel column: Hrs).

title.description: Mention title — usually present for News/Blogs/Web/Podcasts; empty for social media (Excel column: Title).

content.description: Mention body, HTML stripped, truncated to 250 characters. Empty for social media (Excel column: Content).

source.description: Source identifier — usually the mention URL, or `Tweet-ID: ...` for X/Twitter (Excel column: Source).

host.description: Host the mention was found on (Excel column: Domain).

category.description: Lowercase display name of the mention category, e.g. `news`, `instagram`, `x (twitter)` (Excel column: Category).

sentiment.description: Sentiment: `-1` negative, `0` neutral, `1` positive (Excel column: Sentiment).

has_more_mentions.description: True when more results are available beyond this page.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Pass it back as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page; `null` when there are no more pages.

required.description: Keywords that must also appear for the mention to be kept.

excluded.description: Keywords whose presence drops the mention.

items.description: Source token used to identify a mention source category.

mentions_usage_estimation_at_the_end.description: Projected total mentions the account will have consumed by the end of the current billing period, extrapolated from usage so far. Whole number; expressed as a decimal because the projection is computed from a daily rate.
